title: Mean tidal range rose faster at Philadelphia than at Cape May in matched months from 1989-2025
abstract: We tested whether mean tidal range changed faster at Philadelphia than at Cape May. We used fixed NOAA monthly records requested for 1980-2025. Only 423 months passed the joint data checks; 421 were in 1990-2025. A model with month effects, linear time, and an 18.61-year cycle gave a Philadelphia-minus-Cape May trend of 33.89 mm per decade. Its 95% five-year block-wild interval was 26.97 to 40.97 mm per decade. The result stayed positive with other block lengths, no cycle term, a 4.425-year cycle term, and a 1990 start. A check with high water minus low water gave 33.92 mm per decade. The evidence supports a rise in upstream tidal range relative to this coastal gauge under the tested models. It does not identify a cause, measure flood frequency, or establish a steady physical rate. Record gaps, only about two lunar cycles, gauge history, and the error model limit inference. The package includes frozen public-domain source data, hashes, code, results, draws, a figure, and an independent numerical check.

display.caption: Annual means use at least ten matched months. The model uses monthly data. Trend intervals use five-year block-wild errors and the fixed trend design. The annual curve is not steady.
